sample_unit: GP users of ambient AI scribes (of 1003 survey respondents)

links.outcome: GP-reported frequency and severity of errors in ambient scribe notes
links.effect: 32% (n=45) reported errors often/always, including 14% (n=20) with significant-to-critical implications.
links.quote: Errors were common but usually minor: 32% (n=45) reported errors often/always, including 14% (n=20) with significant-to-critical implications.

links.outcome: Ambient scribe error frequency in non-English encounters
links.effect: Errors were most frequent in multiparty consultations (38%), complex histories (35%) and non-English encounters (31%).
links.quote: Errors were most frequent in multiparty consultations (38%), complex histories (35%) and non-English encounters (31%).

links.outcome: GP consent practices before using ambient scribe to record consultations
links.effect: 63% (n=89) routinely sought consent, with ≤10% of patients declining; practices varied.
links.quote: Consent practices varied: 63% (n=89) routinely sought consent, with ≤10% of patients declining.

screen.reason: Mixed-methods survey evaluating real-world GP adoption, error rates, workflow impacts, and consent practices with ambient AI scribes in clinical practice, but does not compare outcomes with vs without a specific guardrail practice.
